t: Nothing of Essex House survives now, but it once stood here as a grand house fronting the Strand. It was built around 1575 for Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, a favourite of Elizabeth the First, and was first called Leicester House. The poet Philip Sidney lived there for a time. After Leicester died in 1588, it passed to his stepson Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, another of the queen's favourites, and took the name Essex House. Much later, the ornithologist James Edmund Harting died here.
